newsitem.title: USA: Senators urge U.S. help for low-income heating.
newsitem.headline: Senators urge U.S. help for low-income heating.

text.p: About half the Senate signed a letter to President Clinton urging him to release $300 million in emergency funds for a program that helps low-income people pay their heating bills, spokesmen for several senators said Friday.
The letter, signed by 48 senators, asked the White House to release immediately $300 million in emergency Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) funds.
The White House was expected to respond within a few days, Senate sources said.
"An emergency condition currently exists because of skyrocketing energy costs and colder than normal temperatures in a large portion of the country," the letter said.
"We urge you to act quickly so that states can make the most efficient use of the funds and can assist families in the traditionally colder months of January and February," it said.
Similar letters have circulated in the last few weeks in the House and Senate.
"Last spring, you authorized the release of $180 million in emergency LIHEAP funds, and this year the need is even greater," the letter. signed by senators of both parties, said.

"In the Northeast and Midwest, the price of home heating oil has jumped at least 22 percent from last year, while natural gas and propane prices in all cold weather states are significantly higher," it said.
